summary: All 8 TDD anchor cases are covered with meaningful, behavior-level assertions and the file mirrors the ValidPasswordValidatorTest precedent (plain JUnit 5, AssertJ, direct validator instantiation, null context). Litmus test passes: each negative case would fail if the implementation regressed to ZoneId.of(tz). The blocking issue is redundant testing — four invalid inputs (GMT+5, +02:00, UT, NotAZone) are asserted twice: once via the @ParameterizedTest offset_or_invalid_returns_false and again via four standalone @Test methods. This is the redundant-testing anti-pattern from the test-master skill (each test must catch a failure no other test catches; here the four explicit methods catch nothing the parameterized test does not). Pick one shape and delete the other. Minor naming-consistency drift on negative-case method names is a style nit.

findings.issue: The @ParameterizedTest offset_or_invalid_returns_false (lines 23-32) iterates over exactly the same four inputs ("GMT+5", "+02:00", "UT", "NotAZone") that are also covered by four separate @Test methods: offset_format_gmt5_returns_false (35-37), offset_format_plus_0200_returns_false (40-42), abbreviation_ut_returns_false (45-47), nonexistent_zone_returns_false (50-52). Every assertion in the four standalone tests is a strict subset of what the parameterized test already verifies — same validator, same inputs, same expected boolean. Removing any one of the four standalone tests would not reduce regression-detection ability by one bit. This violates the test-master rule "each test must justify its existence — it catches a specific failure that no other test catches". The TDD anchor in tasks/1.md happens to name the four cases as separate test methods, but that is a writing convention, not a requirement to also keep a parameterized duplicate. The neighbouring ValidPasswordValidatorTest uses exactly one shape (one @ParameterizedTest for the bag of invalid inputs, plus standalone @Test methods only where each carries a distinct boundary or rationale) — the new test should follow the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Pick one of the two shapes and delete the other. Recommended (matches ValidPasswordValidatorTest precedent and the TDD anchor names verbatim): KEEP the four standalone @Test methods (offset_format_gmt5_returns_false, offset_format_plus_0200_returns_false, abbreviation_ut_returns_false, nonexistent_zone_returns_false) — their explicit names produce readable failure output ("abbreviation_ut_returns_false FAILED" instantly tells you which class of bug regressed) and they map 1:1 to the TDD anchor IDs in tasks/1.md lines 65-68. DELETE lines 23-32 (the @ParameterizedTest plus its imports of ParameterizedTest and ValueSource if no other parameterized test remains). Alternative (less code, one assertion site): KEEP the @ParameterizedTest, DELETE the four standalone methods, and rely on JUnit's per-row test display name to identify which input failed. Either choice closes the finding; do not keep both.

findings.issue: blank_returns_true bundles two distinct assertions (empty string "" and whitespace-only "   ") into a single @Test method. If the first assertion fails, JUnit aborts the method and the whitespace-only case is never evaluated, so a regression that breaks only String.isBlank() handling for whitespace would be reported as "empty string failed" — a misleading failure signal. The TDD anchor at tasks/1.md:70 explicitly names both cases ("\"\" and \"   \" → valid") in one bullet, so collapsing them is defensible, but the blank-detection contract is what's being verified and whitespace-only is the more interesting half (empty string is null-adjacent; whitespace-only is the actual String.isBlank() branch).
findings.recommendation: Either (a) split into two methods — blank_emptyString_returnsTrue_delegatesToNotBlank() and blank_whitespaceOnly_returnsTrue_delegatesToNotBlank() — mirroring the ValidPasswordValidatorTest split between invalid_null_returnsTrue_delegatesToNotBlank (line 41) and invalid_emptyString_returnsTrue_delegatesToNotBlank (line 48), or (b) convert to @ParameterizedTest @ValueSource(strings = {"", "   ", "\t", "\n"}) which adds tab and newline coverage of String.isBlank() at zero extra LoC. Option (a) is the lower-friction match for the existing precedent.

findings.issue: Naming convention drifts from the ValidPasswordValidatorTest precedent. ValidPasswordValidatorTest uses a consistent valid_<scenario>_returnsTrue / invalid_<scenario>_returnsFalse prefix on every method (lines 14, 19, 31, 36, 41, 48). The new test mixes prefixes: valid_iana_kyiv, valid_iana_utc, offset_or_invalid, offset_format_gmt5, abbreviation_ut, nonexistent_zone, null_returns_true, blank_returns_true. Negative cases lack the invalid_ prefix and cannot be filtered with a simple --tests '*invalid*' run. Patterns.md / Testing Requirements should be the single authority on this; if the precedent is the de facto convention, the new test should follow it.
findings.recommendation: Rename negative-case methods to use the invalid_ prefix to match ValidPasswordValidatorTest: invalid_offsetGmt5_returnsFalse, invalid_offsetPlus0200_returnsFalse, invalid_abbreviationUt_returnsFalse, invalid_nonexistentZone_returnsFalse. Rename null_returns_true → valid_null_returnsTrue_delegatesToNotBlank and blank_returns_true → valid_blank_returnsTrue_delegatesToNotBlank (matching ValidPasswordValidatorTest line 41/48 wording, including the _delegatesToNotBlank suffix that documents WHY the answer is true). This is a low-priority polish — the tests work as-is — but it costs nothing and keeps grep/run-by-name patterns uniform across the codebase.
